author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Elena Rybakina recovered from a set down to beat Coco Gauff 3-6, 6-4, 6-4 Thursday night, earning a place in the U.S. Open final against defending champion Aryna Sabalenka.

Gauff took the opening set with disciplined defense and a key service break. Rybakina steadied in the second, used her power to shorten exchanges and forced a deciding set in front of the Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd.

The 27-year-old Kazakh broke for a 5-3 lead in the third set. Gauff immediately broke back, but Rybakina closed the match by breaking serve again. The result keeps Rybakina in contention for a third Grand Slam singles title and sets up a Saturday final against a player seeking a third consecutive U.S. Open championship.

Rybakina is already assured of replacing Sabalenka as world No. 1 after the tournament. Gauff’s loss, following Jessica Pegula’s defeat in the other semifinal, also means no American woman will appear in a Grand Slam final this year, the first season that has happened since 2006.
dek: The incoming world No. 1 recovered from a set down for a 3-6, 6-4, 6-4 semifinal victory and will face defending champion Aryna Sabalenka.
headline: Rybakina rallies past Gauff to reach U.S. Open final
